page: Amazon Web Services c8id.32xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 128 virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

The instance includes 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage as instance store volumes. It supports a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. The CPU architecture integrates advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography features such as AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the c8id.32xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Its memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only operations reaching top-tier status, though single-core CPU performance sits in the average to strong range. The system also excels in data processing, showing top-tier results in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and software compilation.

Given its high compute density, fast DDR5 memory, and large local NVMe storage, this instance is highly cost-efficient for resource-intensive deployments that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for workloads such as high-performance database operations, large-scale software compilation, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference, particularly prompt processing where it achieves top-tier token throughput.
